purpose: Separate the historically distinct sources that later converge around the number 72 so Tempus can study a 72-sector celestial/calendar projection without falsely presenting a composite system as one ancient tradition.
research_conclusion: The proposed 72-sector Tempus map has substantial historical precedents, but no single source establishes the complete modern composite. Jewish seventy-two triplets, Egyptian five-day astrological periods, thirty-six decans, Christian-Kabbalistic angel names, seventy-two zodiacal quinaries, Lenain's five-day genius calendar, the seventy-two Goetic spirits, and later angel-demon pairings are separate strata that must retain provenance.

source_strata.period: rabbinic terminology with later Kabbalistic expansion
source_strata.finding: In ancient tannaitic usage Shem ha-Meforash primarily denotes the distinguished Tetragrammaton. Later Kabbalistic usage includes longer divine-name constructions, including a seventy-two-letter/name tradition.
source_strata.architecture_effect: Do not label every later seventy-two-angel or Goetic overlay as the timeless original meaning of Shem ha-Meforash.

source_strata.period: medieval Jewish commentary and Kabbalistic tradition
source_strata.finding: Rashi describes seventy-two names embedded in Exodus 14:19-21: each verse contains seventy-two letters; the first and third are traversed forward and the middle verse in reverse, producing seventy-two three-letter groups columnwise.
source_strata.architecture_effect: The Jewish root overlay is a seventy-two-triplet/name registry, not a seventy-two-demon registry and not inherently a civil calendar.

source_strata.finding: The verso preserves an astrological calendar based on five-day intervals, with relevant signs or constellations, presiding divinities, influences, signs, and omens. Modern scholarship describes the represented Egyptian calendar as seventy-two five-day half-weeks.
source_strata.architecture_effect: A 72 x 5-day temporal partition has an independent late-antique Egyptian precedent. It must not be retroactively identified with the Jewish seventy-two triplets without separate evidence.

source_strata.source: Testament of Solomon chapter 18; Robert Daniel, Testament of Solomon: Addendum to P.Rain.Cent. 39
source_strata.finding: Chapter 18 presents thirty-six zodiacal decanal spirits; the papyrological study describes each decan as operative for a ten-day period under one of the twelve zodiac signs.
source_strata.architecture_effect: A 36 x 10-day decanal grid is historically distinct from the later 72 x 5-degree angelic quinary grid. Mathematically, one decan can be represented as two five-unit sectors, but that relationship does not prove shared identity.

source_strata.finding: Reuchlin lists the seventy-two triliteral forms and fuller forms using divine endings such as -IAH and -EL, treating the resulting forms as angelic names within Christian Kabbalah.
source_strata.architecture_effect: The pronounceable seventy-two-angel layer is a later Christian-Kabbalistic overlay on the Jewish triplet tradition, not the root registry itself.

source_strata.source: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa, De Occulta Philosophia II.15 and III.25
source_strata.finding: Agrippa explicitly divides each of the twelve zodiac signs into six parts, producing seventy-two 'fives' or celestial quinaries, and places seventy-two angels/names over them; Book III lists the seventy-two angels and connects them to the celestial quinaries.
source_strata.architecture_effect: The 72 x 5-degree zodiacal angular grid is historically attested in Renaissance Christian occultism. Five degrees are established here; five civil days are not established by Agrippa alone.

source_strata.finding: Lenain states that seventy-two geniuses govern seventy-two parts of the circle containing five degrees or five days each; his table runs seventy-two five-day periods from the first degree of Aries and leaves five residual epagomenal days. He also explicitly says that the following calendar tables are his own invention, while drawing the first angelic table from Kircher and Agrippa.
source_strata.architecture_effect: The exact 72 x 5-day genius calendar plus five residual days is a documented historical precedent for the Tempus pentad hypothesis, but it must be labeled a nineteenth-century synthesis rather than ancient Jewish or universally Solomonic doctrine.

source_strata.source: Lemegeton, Part 1: Goetia, Joseph H. Peterson edition from Sloane MS 3825
source_strata.finding: The Ars Goetia presents a catalog of seventy-two spirits. Peterson traces the catalog through the Offices of Spirits / Weyer-Pseudomonarchia stream, where the earlier printed list contains sixty-nine spirits even though the text refers to seventy-two.
source_strata.architecture_effect: The Goetic seventy-two is a separate grimoire lineage. Shared count does not establish origin from the Exodus triplets or from the seventy-two zodiac quinaries.

source_strata.source: Harley MS 6483 and related manuscripts as edited by Stephen Skinner and David Rankine
source_strata.finding: This manuscript tradition pairs each of seventy-two Goetic spirits with the same-numbered Shem angel. Attribution of the compilation to Thomas Rudd is disputed and should remain qualified.
source_strata.architecture_effect: Angel-demon positional pairing is historically attested as a later join, not as Jewish root doctrine and not as an intrinsic property of the base Ars Goetia.

source_strata.source: Nature Communications and large-scale functional-network reviews
source_strata.finding: Contemporary consciousness research models brain function through interacting networks, connectivity, gradients, and multidimensional state spaces. No credible fixed seventy-two-part neural or cognitive ontology was identified in this audit.
source_strata.architecture_effect: Do not present seventy-two angels, spirits, sectors, or names as seventy-two scientifically established brain facets. Premodern microcosmic body correspondences remain historical symbolism, not neuroscience.
